validity.recommendation: Review Status: reclassify 'operating' -> 'construction' unless physical gas flow through the 20-in line is independently confirmed. The Nasiriyah-Gharraf gas-investment (processing) project this line feeds is still under construction as of Dec 2025 with first operations expected Q1 2027.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real and independently corroborated (2+ independent). (1) Ahmed A. Al-Jibawi, 'Shedding Light on Recent Oil & Gas Pipeline Projects in Iraq' (iraqieconomists.net, 2025 PDF): 'In 2023, SCOP completed a 20-inch dry gas pipeline extending from the Gharaf oil field in Dhi Qar Governorate to the 42-inch national dry gas pipeline for 76 km.' (2) al-Mirbad (2 May 2024, Arabic): describes the South Gas Company (شركة غاز الجنوب) Nasiriyah+Gharraf gas project fed by two raw-gas pipelines, the first '20-inch (عشرين عقدة) from the Gharraf field with capacity 120 MMcf/d (مقمق)' and a second 14-inch/80 MMcf/d line from the Nasiriyah field. Not a phantom, not a duplicate of any roster row (no other Gharraf/Rifai/Nasiriyah-field gas feed line; P1851/P1852 are Rumaila/Trans-Iraq->Nasiriyah, distinct). CLASSIFICATION: correct as gas transmission — Jibawi says it ties the field into the 42-in NATIONAL dry gas trunk; Fuel=Gas correct; not an oil/NGL line (none of the GulfPub crude roster matches). SPEC CHECK vs GEM: Diameter 20-in CONFIRMED by BOTH al-Mirbad and Jibawi (high). Length 76 km CONFIRMED by Jibawi (medium; al-Mirbad does not state a length). Capacity 120 MMcf/d CONFIRMED by al-Mirbad (matches the ~130 MMcf/d Gharraf-field contribution cited in aggregate reporting). Owner 'Iraq Ministry of Oil' defensible — built by SCOP (State Company for Oil Projects) and operated under South Gas Company, both Ministry of Oil entities (could be refined to 'South Gas Company'). THE CONCERN — STATUS: GEM says 'operating' (updated 2025-07-18) but the sheet's own cited al-Mirbad source (May 2024) describes the project at 'advanced stages — equipment installation and mechanical works, connecting equipment and internal pipe networks', i.e. UNDER CONSTRUCTION, and does NOT support 'operating' (the worklist ref-check already flagged al-Mirbad lacked 'operating'). Independent Egypt Oil & Gas (23 Dec 2025) states the Nasiriyah & Gharraf gas project (200 MMscf/d, South Gas Company + Baker Hughes) is 'under development' with initial operations 'expected in Q1 2027'. This 20-in/120-MMcf/d line is the RAW FEED line into that not-yet-operating processing complex per al-Mirbad. There is a genuine source conflict: Jibawi says the 76-km pipe itself was completed in 2023 (so the pipe may physically exist and could evacuate field gas), but two independent sources indicate the system it serves is not operating until 2027. Net: 'operating' is not clearly supported; flag for status review, do not silently pass.

routes.corridor_desc: The 20-in line runs ~76 km from the Gharraf oil field (which sources place 5 km NW of Al-Rifa'i, 9 km SE of Qalat Sukkar, and 85 km N of Nasiriyah) generally SOUTH down the Al-Rifa'i / Qalat Sukkar corridor toward Nasiriyah, tying into the 42-in national dry gas trunk. Start is defensible from the named field location relative to Al-Rifa'i (sourced coords 31.72079,46.10778). The exact tie-in / end point is NOT sourced: end coords are an INFERRED terminus placed in the Nasiriyah vicinity from the stated 76-km length and southward geography — treat as a loose bound, not a surveyed point.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints established from Jibawi (origin = Gharraf oil field, Dhi Qar; destination = 42-in national dry gas pipeline; length 76 km) and al-Mirbad (raw-gas feed from Gharraf field into the Nasiriyah/South Gas Company complex). Start coord derived from the field's sourced position relative to Al-Rifa'i (31.72079,46.10778); NOT fabricated. End coord is an inferred Nasiriyah-area terminus (76-km southward from the field) — flagged low/loose because the precise national-grid tie-in point is not independently sourced. Waypoint Al-Rifa'i coords are sourced. No route geometry edited; this is a suggestion set only.

summary: P5856 Gharraf Gas Pipeline is real and correctly a gas transmission line (dia 20in, len 76km, cap 120 MMcf/d all corroborated), but STATUS 'operating' is a concern — the Nasiriyah-Gharraf gas project it feeds is under construction (al-Mirbad 2024, Egypt Oil&Gas Dec-2025: first ops Q1 2027).
